question:
Which is the only muscle in the human body that is NOT attached at both the ends?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Adductor
Tongue
Biceps
Triceps
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tongue

Explanation:
The tongue is the only muscle in the human body that is NOT attached at both ends. It is a free-moving muscle attached at only one end, while the other end remains free. The tongue consists of 8 intrinsic muscles that allow it to move in various directions. This muscle plays a crucial role in chewing, swallowing, and speaking. Other options like adductor, biceps, and triceps are all attached at both ends.

Extra Facts:
The tongue is one of the strongest muscles in the human body. It contains over 10,000 taste buds that help in recognizing different flavors. The tongue muscles control both voluntary and involuntary movements. Additionally, the unique structure of the tongue aids in sound production.

question:
Identify a muscle responsible for the exit of waste material from the body.

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Rectus
Pectoralis
Sphincter
Gastrocnemius
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sphincter

Explanation:
The Sphincter is a specialized muscle responsible for controlling the exit of waste materials from the body. It is a ring-shaped muscle that regulates the opening and closing of various body orifices through its contraction and relaxation. For example, the External Anal Sphincter located at the end of the Rectum controls the expulsion of feces. Similarly, the urethral sphincter muscles regulate the release of urine. Sphincters play a crucial role in maintaining bodily functions by ensuring controlled release of waste and other substances.

Extra Facts:
1. There are two types of sphincters in the human body: Involuntary and Voluntary. Involuntary sphincters function automatically, while voluntary sphincters are under conscious control.
2. The Heart contains sphincter muscles that regulate blood flow.
3. In the Digestive System, sphincter muscles are vital for controlling the passage of food and digestive juices, aiding in digestion and absorption.

☛ What type of muscle is the External Anal Sphincter? → Voluntary muscle
☛ Which muscle controls urine excretion? → Urethral Sphincter
☛ What is the function of sphincter muscles in the heart? → Regulate blood flow
☛ What is the shape of sphincter muscles? → Ring-shaped

question:
Muscle cells and muscle fibres are developed from embryonic precursor cells known as:

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: myoblasts
myocyte
myofibril
myonuclei
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is myoblasts

Explanation:
Muscle cells and muscle fibres are developed from embryonic precursor cells known as 'myoblasts'. These cells are specifically responsible for muscle development. Myoblasts divide and fuse together to form multinucleated muscle fibers called 'myotubes', which later mature into muscle cells (myocytes). This process occurs during embryonic development and is also crucial for muscle repair in adults. 'Myocyte' refers to a mature muscle cell, while 'myofibril' is the structural unit of muscle fibers, and 'myonuclei' are the nuclei within muscle cells.

Extra Facts:
Muscle development (myogenesis) is a complex process involving various genes and proteins. Myoblasts are regulated by 'myogenic regulatory factors (MRFs)' such as MyoD, Myf5, myogenin, and MRF4. These factors control the differentiation and fusion of myoblasts. In adults, 'satellite cells' play a vital role in muscle repair and regeneration. These cells are similar to myoblasts and become activated after injury to form new muscle cells.

☛ Which proteins are responsible for muscle contraction? → Actin and myosin
☛ What are the muscles of the heart called? → Cardiac muscle
☛ What is the immediate source of energy in muscles? → ATP
☛ What causes muscle fatigue? → Accumulation of lactic acid

मांसपेशी कोशिकाएं और मांसपेशी रेशे भ्रूणीय पूर्ववर्ती कोशिकाओं (embryonic precursor cells) से विकसित होते हैं जिन्हें ___________ कहा जाता है।

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: पेशीकोरक (myoblasts)

पेशी केंद्रक (myonuclei)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पेशीकोरक (myoblasts)

Explanation:
मांसपेशी कोशिकाएं और मांसपेशी रेशे भ्रूणीय पूर्ववर्ती कोशिकाओं से विकसित होते हैं जिन्हें 'पेशीकोरक (myoblasts)' कहा जाता है। ये कोशिकाएं विशेष रूप से मांसपेशियों के विकास के लिए जिम्मेदार होती हैं। पेशीकोरक कोशिकाएं विभाजित होकर एक-दूसरे से जुड़ जाती हैं और बहुकेंद्रकीय मांसपेशी तंतु (myotubes) बनाती हैं, जो बाद में परिपक्व मांसपेशी कोशिकाओं (myocytes) में विकसित हो जाती हैं। यह प्रक्रिया भ्रूण के विकास के दौरान होती है और वयस्कों में मांसपेशियों की मरम्मत के लिए भी महत्वपूर्ण है। 'पेशीअणु (myocyte)' एक परिपक्व मांसपेशी कोशिका है, जबकि 'पेशी तंतुक (myofibril)' मांसपेशी तंतु की संरचनात्मक इकाई है और 'पेशी केंद्रक (myonuclei)' मांसपेशी कोशिकाओं के केंद्रक होते हैं।

Extra Facts:
मांसपेशी विकास (myogenesis) एक जटिल प्रक्रिया है जिसमें विभिन्न जीन और प्रोटीन शामिल होते हैं। पेशीकोरक कोशिकाएं 'मायोजेनिक रेगुलेटरी फैक्टर्स (MRFs)' जैसे MyoD, Myf5, myogenin और MRF4 द्वारा नियंत्रित होती हैं। ये कारक पेशीकोरक कोशिकाओं के विभेदन (differentiation) और संलयन (fusion) को नियंत्रित करते हैं। वयस्कों में, 'सैटेलाइट कोशिकाएं (satellite cells)' मांसपेशियों की मरम्मत और पुनर्जनन में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती हैं। ये कोशिकाएं पेशीकोरक के समान होती हैं और चोट के बाद सक्रिय होकर नई मांसपेशी कोशिकाएं बनाती हैं।

question:
Myosin and actin are -

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Muscle protein
Muscle carbohydrate
Muscle fat
Muscle enzymes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Muscle protein

Explanation:
Myosin and actin are two major proteins found in muscles that are responsible for muscle contraction. These proteins are present in muscle fibers and function according to the Sliding Filament Theory. Actin forms thin filaments, while myosin forms thick filaments. During muscle contraction, myosin slides over actin, causing the muscle to shorten. This process is powered by the hydrolysis of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate).

Extra Facts:
Calcium ions (Ca2+) play a crucial role in muscle contraction by activating the troponin-tropomyosin complex. The sarcomere is the structural and functional unit of muscle fibers where actin and myosin are located. Myosin has the ability to form cross-bridges, which bind to actin and enable contraction. These proteins are found not only in skeletal muscles but also in cardiac and smooth muscles. The interaction between actin and myosin is regulated by proteins like troponin and tropomyosin.

☛ What is the heart muscle called? → Cardiac muscle
☛ What type of filament does myosin form? → Thick filament

मायोसिन और एक्टिन क्या हैं?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: मांसपेशीय प्रोटीन
मांसपेशीय कार्बोहाइड्रेट
मांसपेशीय वसा
मांसपेशीय एंजाइम
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मांसपेशीय प्रोटीन

Explanation:
मायोसिन और एक्टिन मांसपेशियों में पाए जाने वाले दो प्रमुख प्रोटीन हैं जो मांसपेशी संकुचन (Muscle Contraction) के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं। ये प्रोटीन मांसपेशी फाइबर (Muscle Fibers) में पाए जाते हैं और स्लाइडिंग फिलामेंट थ्योरी (Sliding Filament Theory) के अनुसार कार्य करते हैं। एक्टिन पतले फिलामेंट्स (Thin Filaments) बनाता है, जबकि मायोसिन मोटे फिलामेंट्स (Thick Filaments) का निर्माण करता है। मांसपेशी संकुचन के दौरान, मायोसिन एक्टिन पर सरकता है, जिससे मांसपेशी छोटी हो जाती है। यह प्रक्रिया एटीपी (ATP) के हाइड्रोलिसिस द्वारा संचालित होती है।

Extra Facts:
मांसपेशी संकुचन में कैल्शियम आयन (Ca2+) की महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका होती है, जो ट्रोपोनिन-ट्रोपोमायोसिन कॉम्प्लेक्स को सक्रिय करता है। सार्कोमियर (Sarcomere) मांसपेशी फाइबर की संरचनात्मक और कार्यात्मक इकाई है, जहाँ एक्टिन और मायोसिन पाए जाते हैं। मायोसिन में क्रॉस-ब्रिज (Cross-Bridge) बनाने की क्षमता होती है, जो एक्टिन से जुड़कर संकुचन को संभव बनाता है। ये प्रोटीन न केवल कंकाल (Skeletal) मांसपेशियों में, बल्कि हृदय (Cardiac) और चिकनी (Smooth) मांसपेशियों में भी पाए जाते हैं।

question:
How do the muscle cells help in movement?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options: The thickness of the cell layer helps in movement.
The lining of the vessels inside help in movement.
The blood flow of the cells helps in movement.
The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.

Explanation:
Muscle cells (myocytes) help in movement through their ability to contract and relax. This process occurs due to the interaction between two protein filaments—actin and myosin. When a signal is received from the brain, these filaments slide over each other, causing the muscle to contract. This contraction pulls on the bones, resulting in movement of body parts. During relaxation, the muscles return to their original length. Thus, the alternating contraction and relaxation of muscle cells are the basis of movement.

Extra Facts:
1. There are three types of muscles: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth. Skeletal muscles are voluntary (controlled consciously), while cardiac and smooth muscles are involuntary.
2. ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) provides energy for muscle contraction.
3. Muscle fatigue occurs due to the accumulation of lactic acid, which is produced during anaerobic respiration (lack of oxygen).

☛ Which proteins are responsible for muscle contraction? → Actin and myosin

☛ Which muscles are voluntary? → Skeletal muscles

पेशीय कोशिकाएँ (मांसपेशियों की कोशिकाएँ) गति करने में मदद करती हैं क्योंकि ये संकुचन (contraction) और विश्राम (relaxation) की क्रिया करती हैं। यह प्रक्रिया एक्टिन (actin) और मायोसिन (myosin) प्रोटीन फिलामेंट्स की परस्पर क्रिया के कारण होती है। जब मांसपेशियों को मस्तिष्क से संकेत मिलता है, तो ये प्रोटीन फिलामेंट्स एक-दूसरे पर स्लाइड करते हैं, जिससे मांसपेशियों का संकुचन होता है। इस संकुचन के कारण हड्डियाँ खिंचती या सिकुड़ती हैं, जिससे शरीर के अंगों में गति होती है। विश्राम की अवस्था में मांसपेशियाँ अपनी सामान्य लंबाई में वापस आ जाती हैं। इस प्रकार, पेशीय कोशिकाओं का संकुचन और विश्राम ही गति का मुख्य आधार है।

Extra Facts:
1. मांसपेशियाँ तीन प्रकार की होती हैं: रेखित (skeletal), हृदय (cardiac), और अरेखित (smooth)। रेखित मांसपेशियाँ स्वैच्छिक (voluntary) होती हैं और इन्हें हम नियंत्रित कर सकते हैं, जबकि हृदय और अरेखित मांसपेशियाँ अनैच्छिक (involuntary) होती हैं।
2. एटीपी (ATP) मांसपेशियों के संकुचन के लिए ऊर्जा प्रदान करता है।
3. मांसपेशियों का थकान (fatigue) लैक्टिक अम्ल (lactic acid) के जमाव के कारण होता है, जो ऑक्सीजन की कमी के दौरान उत्पन्न होता है।

question:
In which part of the human body will you find the 'superior rectus'?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Ear
Eye
Nose
Tongue
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Eye.

Explanation:
The 'superior rectus' is a muscle found in the human eye. It is responsible for elevating the eye (upward movement) and adducting it (inward movement). This muscle is attached to the eyeball and is controlled by the oculomotor nerve (cranial nerve III). The eye has six extraocular muscles in total, which include the superior rectus, inferior rectus, medial rectus, lateral rectus, superior oblique, and inferior oblique. These muscles work together to control eye movements and maintain stable vision by coordinating the position of the eyes.

Extra Facts:
The human eye is a highly complex organ. The extraocular muscles not only stabilize vision but also ensure binocular vision (coordination between both eyes). Weakness or paralysis of the superior rectus muscle can lead to difficulty in elevating the eye, a condition known as 'superior rectus palsy', which may cause diplopia (double vision). The study of these muscles is crucial in fields like Ophthalmology and Neurology. The superior rectus is one of the four rectus muscles, which are named based on their positions (superior, inferior, medial, and lateral).

question:
Muscles are of three types. Which of the following is NOT one of them ?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Sesamoids
Smooth
Cardiac
Skeletal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sesamoids

Explanation:
Human muscles are classified into three types: Smooth muscles (involuntary muscles, found in organs like intestines), Cardiac muscles (found only in the heart), and Skeletal muscles (voluntary muscles attached to bones). Sesamoids are a type of bone, not muscle tissue. These bones are embedded within tendons and help reduce friction, such as the patella (kneecap, which is a sesamoid bone). Therefore, sesamoids are not a type of muscular tissue.

Extra Facts:
Smooth muscles are found in internal organs like the digestive tract, blood vessels, and bladder. They are involuntary and function automatically. Cardiac muscles are exclusive to the heart and have self-contracting properties. Skeletal muscles are voluntary and can be controlled consciously. They are attached to bones and facilitate body movement. Sesamoid bones are small, round bones embedded in tendons, reducing joint pressure and improving mechanical efficiency.

question:
Why does one get cramps after sudden physical activity?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: The build-up of hydrochloric acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps.
The pepsin enzyme releases chemicals that lead to cramps.
The oxygen molecules breaks down.
The build-up of lactic acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The build-up of lactic acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps.

Explanation:
When we engage in sudden physical activity, our muscles require more oxygen for energy. If the oxygen supply is insufficient, the muscles start anaerobic respiration. In this process, glucose undergoes incomplete oxidation, leading to the production of lactic acid. The accumulation of lactic acid in the muscles causes pain and cramps. This is a normal biochemical process that occurs during intense physical activity.

Extra Facts:
Muscle cramps are not only caused by lactic acid but can also result from electrolyte imbalance, dehydration, and overuse of muscles. Cramps commonly occur in the legs, arms, or abdominal muscles. Regular exercise and proper hydration can help prevent cramps. The buildup of lactic acid usually subsides on its own after some time when the body receives sufficient oxygen.

Extra Facts:

question:
When there is a lack of oxygen in our muscle cells, the breakdown of pyruvate takes place and it is converted into

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: lactic acid and energy
carbon dioxide and water
water and energy
ethanol and carbon dioxide
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is lactic acid and energy

Explanation:
When there is a lack of oxygen in muscle cells, pyruvate undergoes anaerobic respiration, converting into lactic acid along with a small amount of energy (ATP). This process, known as lactic acid fermentation, occurs in humans and animals, leading to muscle fatigue and pain. Unlike aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration produces only 2 ATP molecules per glucose molecule.

Extra Facts:
There are two types of anaerobic respiration:
1. Lactic Acid Fermentation (in animals and humans)
2. Alcoholic Fermentation (in yeast and some bacteria, producing ethanol and CO2).
Aerobic respiration yields 36-38 ATP, while anaerobic respiration is less efficient. Lactic acid buildup causes muscle cramps during intense exercise.

जब मांसपेशियों की कोशिकाओं में ऑक्सीजन की कमी होती है, तो पायरूवेट का विखंडन अवायवीय श्वसन (Anaerobic Respiration) के द्वारा होता है। इस प्रक्रिया में पायरूवेट लैक्टिक अम्ल (Lactic Acid) में परिवर्तित हो जाता है और साथ ही थोड़ी मात्रा में ऊर्जा (ATP) उत्पन्न होती है। यह प्रक्रिया मांसपेशियों में थकान और दर्द का कारण बनती है। यह मानव शरीर में होने वाली लैक्टिक अम्ल किण्वन (Lactic Acid Fermentation) का एक उदाहरण है।

Extra Facts:
अवायवीय श्वसन दो प्रकार का होता है:
1. लैक्टिक अम्ल किण्वन (मनुष्य और जंतुओं में)

वायवीय श्वसन की तुलना में अवायवीय श्वसन से कम ऊर्जा (2 ATP) प्राप्त होती है, जबकि वायवीय श्वसन से 36-38 ATP प्राप्त होते हैं।

question:
Participation in which of the following activities is NOT recommended for the motor development of a student?

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: Playing cricket
Joining a dance class
Attending Yoga sessions
Helping the visually challenge
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Helping the visually challenge

Explanation:
Motor development refers to the physical growth and strengthening of a child's muscles and coordination. Activities like playing cricket, joining a dance class, and attending yoga sessions enhance physical mobility, balance, flexibility, and muscle development. However, 'helping the visually challenged' is a social or assistance-based activity that does not directly contribute to motor development. It primarily improves empathy and social sensitivity rather than physical skills.

Extra Facts:
Motor development is categorized into two types:
1. Gross Motor Development: Involves large muscle movements like running, jumping, or throwing a ball.
2. Fine Motor Development: Involves small muscle movements like writing, drawing, or buttoning clothes.
Activities like yoga and dance improve both types of motor skills.

question:
Movement in most of the animals is a coordinated activity of which of the following systems?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Only skeletal and nervous systems
Only muscular system
Muscular, skeletal and nervous systems
Only nervous system
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Muscular, skeletal and nervous systems

Explanation:
Movement in animals is a complex process that involves the coordinated activity of three major systems: muscular system, skeletal system, and nervous system. Muscles generate movement through contraction and relaxation. The skeletal system (bones) provides a framework to which muscles are attached and offers the necessary support for movement. The nervous system controls muscle contraction and relaxation by sending signals to the muscles. The proper coordination of these three systems enables smooth and controlled movement.

Extra Facts:
Muscles are of three types: skeletal (striated), cardiac, and smooth muscles. Skeletal muscles are responsible for voluntary movement, while smooth and cardiac muscles control involuntary movement. Nervous system includes motor neurons that transmit signals to the muscles. Skeletal system not only aids in movement but also provides shape and protection to the body.

question:
Breakdown of pyruvate into lactic acid and energy in lack of Oxygen takes place in which of the following ?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Bacteria
Mitochondria
Yeast
Human muscle cells
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Human muscle cells

Explanation:
The conversion of pyruvate into lactic acid and energy occurs during anaerobic respiration, which takes place in the absence of oxygen. This process primarily occurs in human muscle cells when oxygen supply is insufficient during intense physical activity. In this process, glucose undergoes partial oxidation, producing 2 ATP molecules and lactic acid. The accumulation of lactic acid causes muscle fatigue. This process occurs in the cytoplasm, not in mitochondria.

Extra Facts:
◼ Anaerobic respiration is of two types: Lactic acid fermentation (in human muscles) and Alcoholic fermentation (in yeast).
◼ In yeast, pyruvate is converted into ethanol and CO2, which is used in bread-making and alcohol production.
◼ In mitochondria, pyruvate undergoes complete oxidation, producing 36 ATP molecules (aerobic respiration).
◼ Bacteria can also perform anaerobic respiration, but they may produce other byproducts (e.g., propionic acid) instead of lactic acid.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ How many ATP are produced in aerobic respiration? → 36 ATP
☛ Where does lactic acid fermentation occur? → Human muscle cells
☛ What is the primary function of mitochondria? → ATP production
☛ What happens to glucose in anaerobic respiration? → Partial oxidation

पायरूवेट का लेक्टिक अम्ल और ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन अवायवीय श्वसन की प्रक्रिया में होता है, जो ऑक्सीजन की अनुपस्थिति में होता है। यह प्रक्रिया मुख्य रूप से मानव पेशी कोशिकाओं में होती है, जब तीव्र शारीरिक गतिविधि के दौरान ऑक्सीजन की आपूर्ति अपर्याप्त हो जाती है। इस प्रक्रिया में ग्लूकोज का आंशिक ऑक्सीकरण होता है, जिससे 2 ATP अणु उत्पन्न होते हैं और लेक्टिक अम्ल बनता है। लेक्टिक अम्ल का संचय पेशियों में थकान का कारण बनता है। यह प्रक्रिया कोशिका द्रव्य (साइटोप्लाज्म) में होती है, न कि माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया में।

question:
Muscles are of three types. Which of the following is NOT one of them ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Sesamoids
Smooth
Cardiac
Skeletal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sesamoids

Explanation:
The human body has three types of muscles: Smooth Muscles, Cardiac Muscles, and Skeletal Muscles. Smooth muscles are found in organs and blood vessels and are involuntary. Cardiac muscles are found only in the heart and are also involuntary. Skeletal muscles are attached to bones and are voluntary. Sesamoids are a type of bone, not a muscle. They are found in tendons, such as the patella (kneecap).

Extra Facts:
The primary functions of muscles are to provide movement, maintain posture, and control organ activities. Smooth muscles are found in the digestive system, bladder, and blood vessels. Cardiac muscles contract automatically and regulate the heartbeat. Skeletal muscles constitute about 40% of body weight and help in moving joints.

Solution: Correct Answer is Ligament

Explanation:
A ligament is a flexible, strong, and fibrous connective tissue that attaches bone to bone. It provides stability to joints and controls their movement. Ligaments are made of collagen protein and have high tensile strength. They prevent excessive joint movement and protect against injuries. For example, the ACL (Anterior Cruciate Ligament) in the knee is a major ligament that connects the thigh bone (femur) to the shin bone (tibia).

Extra Facts:
☛ Tendons connect muscles to bones, while ligaments connect bones to bones.
☛ Cartilage is a flexible tissue that reduces friction in joints and acts as a shock absorber.
☛ An injury to a ligament is called a sprain, whereas an injury to a tendon or muscle is called a strain.
☛ The strongest ligament in the human body is the iliofemoral ligament, which stabilizes the hip joint.

Explanation:
अस्थि-बंधन (Ligament) एक लचीला, मजबूत और रेशेदार संयोजी ऊतक होता है जो हड्डी को हड्डी से जोड़ता है। यह जोड़ों को स्थिरता प्रदान करता है और उनकी गति को नियंत्रित करता है। अस्थि-बंधन प्रोटीन कोलेजन से बने होते हैं और इनमें उच्च तन्य शक्ति होती है। ये जोड़ों को अत्यधिक गति से बचाते हैं और चोटों को रोकते हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, घुटने का 'एसीएल' (Anterior Cruciate Ligament) एक प्रमुख अस्थि-बंधन है जो जांघ की हड्डी को पिंडली की हड्डी से जोड़ता है।

question:
You get cramps after participating in a 400 m race. Which option best explains the reason for the same?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Lack of oxygen and pyruvate is converted to glucose
Lack of oxygen and pyruvate is converted to ethanol
Enough oxygen and pyruvate converted to lactic acid
Lack of oxygen and pyruvate converted to lactic acid
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lack of oxygen and pyruvate converted to lactic acid

Explanation:
A 400-meter race is an intense activity requiring rapid energy production in muscles. During such high-intensity exercise, the body's oxygen supply becomes insufficient, forcing cells to switch to anaerobic respiration. In anaerobic respiration, glucose undergoes partial breakdown, and pyruvate is converted into lactic acid. The accumulation of lactic acid in muscles causes cramps and fatigue, a condition known as muscle fatigue. This process is temporary, and lactic acid is later metabolized when oxygen becomes available.

Extra Facts:
1. Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide instead of lactic acid, a process called fermentation.
2. Lactic acid buildup is common after strenuous exercise and is gradually reconverted to pyruvate in the presence of oxygen.
3. Proper hydration and stretching can help reduce muscle cramps caused by lactic acid accumulation.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is pyruvate converted into during anaerobic respiration? → Lactic acid
☛ What are the byproducts of fermentation in yeast? → Ethanol and CO₂
☛ What causes muscle fatigue during intense exercise? → Lactic acid accumulation
☛ Where does aerobic respiration occur? → Mitochondria
☛ Which process does not require oxygen? → Anaerobic respiration

400 मीटर की दौड़ में भाग लेने के बाद आपको ऐंठन होती है। कौन सा विकल्प इसका सबसे सटीक कारण बताता है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: ऑक्सीजन की कमी और पाइरूवेट का ग्लूकोज में परिवर्तन
ऑक्सीजन की कमी और पाइरूवेट का एथेनॉल में परिवर्तन
ऑक्सीजन की पर्याप्त उपस्थिति और पाइरूवेट का लैक्टिक अम्ल में परिवर्तन
ऑक्सीजन की कमी और पाइरूवेट का लैक्टिक अम्ल में परिवर्तन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है ऑक्सीजन की कमी और पाइरूवेट का लैक्टिक अम्ल में परिवर्तन

Explanation:
400 मीटर की दौड़ एक तीव्र गति वाली गतिविधि है जिसमें मांसपेशियों को अधिक ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है। इस दौरान, शरीर में ऑक्सीजन की आपूर्ति अपर्याप्त हो जाती है, जिसके कारण कोशिकाएं अवायवीय श्वसन (Anaerobic Respiration) की ओर मुड़ जाती हैं। अवायवीय श्वसन में, ग्लूकोज का आंशिक विघटन होता है और पाइरूवेट लैक्टिक अम्ल (Lactic Acid) में परिवर्तित हो जाता है। लैक्टिक अम्ल का संचय मांसपेशियों में ऐंठन (Cramps) और थकान का कारण बनता है। यह प्रक्रिया मांसपेशीय थकान (Muscle Fatigue) का एक प्रमुख कारण है।

Extra Facts:
1. अवायवीय श्वसन यीस्ट (Yeast) में भी होता है, लेकिन वहाँ पाइरूवेट, एथेनॉल और कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड में परिवर्तित होता है, जिसे किण्वन (Fermentation) कहते हैं।
2. लैक्टिक अम्ल का संचय अक्सर तीव्र व्यायाम के बाद होता है और यह शरीर द्वारा धीरे-धीरे ऑक्सीजन की उपस्थिति में पुनः पाइरूवेट में बदल जाता है।
3. मांसपेशियों में ऐंठन को कम करने के लिए हल्की स्ट्रेचिंग और हाइड्रेशन महत्वपूर्ण है।
